'''Radhe Shyam Agarwal''' (also known as '''R S Agarwal''') is an Indian entrepreneur, co-founder and executive chairman of [[Emami]], a global group of company engaged in the business of [[Fast Moving Consumer Goods|FMCG]], paper, [[real estate]], edible oils, health care and cement.<ref>{{cite news|title=Passing on the baton at Emami family|url=http://profit.ndtv.com/news/market/article-passing-on-the-baton-at-emami-family-42199|accessdate=3 March 2015|publisher=NDTV}}</ref> Radhe is among the top 100 richest Indians<ref>{{cite news|title=Radhe Shyam Agarwal|url=http://forbesindia.com/richprofile/radhe-shyam-agarwal/166|accessdate=3 March 2015|work=Forbes India|archive-date=2 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402133713/http://forbesindia.com/richprofile/radhe-shyam-agarwal/166|url-status=dead}}</ref> and was listed by ''[[Forbes]]'' as having a net worth of $1.43 billion in 2015.<ref>{{cite news |title=Radhe Shyam Agarwal |url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/radhe-shyam-agarwal/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131102204916/https://www.forbesindia.com/richprofile/radhe-shyam-agarwal/166 |archive-date=2013-11-02 |accessdate=3 March 2015 |work=Forbes}}</ref>

==Early life==
Radhe was born in a [[Marwari people|Marwari]] family on 18 February 1946 in [[Kolkata]], [[India]]. Radhe completed his college education from [[St. Xavier's College, Kolkata|St. Xavier's College]], [[Kolkata]]. He got his [[Bachelor of Laws|LLB]] from [[Calcutta University]], and M.Com from [[Calcutta University]]. Radhe is a [[Chartered Accountant]] from [[Institute of Chartered Accountants of India]] and [[Company Secretary]] from [[Institute of Company Secretaries of India]]. In 1970 Radhe joined [[Aditya Birla Group]] as vice president.<ref>{{cite news|title=Tale Of Two Families|url=https://www.forbes.com/global/2011/0808/companies-emami-shyam-goenka-radhe-shyam-two-families.html|accessdate=3 March 2015|work=Forbes}}</ref>

==Emami==
In 1974 Radhe along with his school friend [[Radhe Shyam Goenka]], started a cosmetics company [[Emami]]. The company was started with a capital of $2600 borrowed from Radhe Shyam Goenka's father.<ref>{{cite news|title=Breakfast with BS: Radhe Shyam Agarwal & Radhe Shyam Goenka|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/opinion/breakfast-with-bs-radhe-shyam-agarwal-radhe-shyam-goenka-110102600016_1.html|accessdate=3 March 2015|publisher=Business Standard}}</ref> Emami is now a multiple business global group of companies with a [[revenue]] of above $1.3 billion.<ref>{{cite news|title=Tale Of Two Families|url=https://www.forbes.com/global/2011/0808/companies-emami-shyam-goenka-radhe-shyam-two-families.html|accessdate=3 March 2015|work=Forbes}} Some of the famous products by Emami are "He", "Fair and Handsome", "Navratan Hair Oil"</ref>

==Associations==
Radhe also serves as Joint Chairman and Director of Emami group of companies, Executive Director of Emami, and Director of Zandu Realty. He had also served as Director of West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation and Trustee of Merchant Chamber of Commerce and Industries.<ref>{{cite news|title=Agarwal Radhe|url=http://in.reuters.com/finance/stocks/officerProfile?symbol=EMAM.BO&officerId=731006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402132623/http://in.reuters.com/finance/stocks/officerProfile?symbol=EMAM.BO&officerId=731006|url-status=dead|archive-date=2 April 2015|accessdate=3 March 2015|publisher=Reuters}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Radhe is married to Usha Bansal and has two sons, Aditya Agarwal and Harsh Agarwal, and one daughter, Priti Agarwal Sureka.<ref>{{cite news|title=Relationship of equals|url=http://businesstoday.intoday.in/story/family-business-emami-group/1/17173.html|accessdate=3 March 2015|publisher=Business Today}}</ref> The entire family is part of the Emami group and lives on tony Southern Avenue in [[Kolkata]], [[India]]. Priti Agarwal is married to Raj Sureka.<ref>{{cite news|title=Emami Promoters Are Friends in Deed|url=http://www.moneycontrol.com/sme-stepup/news/emami_promoters_are_friends_in_deed-786979.html|accessdate=3 March 2015|publisher=Money Control}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Thicker than water|url=http://businesstoday.intoday.in/story/family-business-thrive-in-india-fortis-religare-jubilant/1/212399.html|accessdate=3 March 2015|publisher=Business Today}}</ref>

==Criminal charges==
In the early morning of 9 December 2011, an [[AMRI Hospitals|AMRI Hospital]] in south Kolkata's Dhakuria district erupted in fire, leading to the deaths of 92 people — mostly critically ill patients, many of them suffocating in their sleep.<ref name="IANS2016">{{cite news|title=AMRI Hospital tragedy: Kolkata court frames charges|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/cities/kolkata/amri-hospital-tragedy-kolkata-court-frames-charges-2887133/|access-date=29 August 2016|work=Indian Express|agency=[[Indo-Asian News Service]]|date=1 July 2016}}</ref> The following day, the license for the hospital was cancelled, and the Chief Minister of [[West Bengal]] ordered a judicial inquiry into the incident.<ref name="NDTV2011">{{cite news |last1= |date=10 December 2011 |title=Kolkata hospital fire: Mamata Banerjee orders judicial inquiry |url=http://www.ndtv.com/india-news/kolkata-hospital-fire-mamata-banerjee-orders-judicial-inquiry-566949 |accessdate=29 August 2016 |work=[[NDTV]] |publisher=NDTV Convergence Limited}}</ref> Allegedly, the fire was triggered by flammable chemicals that were stored at the site.<ref name="NDTV2011"/><ref name="EconTimes2011">[http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics/nation/amri-hospital-fire-emami-boss-rs-goenka-and-partner-sk-todi-among-6-held/articleshow/11052168.cms], Economic Times, 10 December 2011</ref> Rescue efforts were hampered by the narrowness and congestion of the road leading to the hospital,<ref name="NDTV2011"/> and the allegations that all of the windows and doors were locked<ref name="NDTV2011"/> and that the fire alarms and sprinklers installed at the hospital did not work during the fire.<ref name="EconTimes2011"/>

Seven members of the hospital's board were arrested the same day, and were remanded to police custody until 20 December by the court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate in [[Alipore]].<ref name="NDTV2011"/> Among the seven arrested were Agarwal and Goenka, founders of Emami and directors of the hospital chain, who were charged with negligently causing the deaths.<ref name="NDTV2011"/> Ultimately a total of 16 people stood accused in the courts in July 2016, including the board members and several directors of the hospital.<ref name="IANS2016"/> Amongst the charges were culpable homicide not amounting to murder under section 304 of the Indian Penal Code, which carries a maximum sentence of 10 years imprisonment in cases where the criminal actions are undertaken knowingly but without the intention to cause death.<ref name="IANS2016"/> Additional charges were laid under Section 308 (attempt to commit culpable homicide) and Section 38 (effect caused partly by act and partly by omission).<ref name="IANS2016"/>

The fire was recorded as the largest hospital tragedy in India at the time.<ref name="EconTimes2011"/>
